question.text:
Find the truth set of $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $\mathbb{R}{:}$

  • $P(x):$ $4x - 7 \geq 9$

  • $Q(x):$ $ 0 \lt x \lt 5$
question.explanation:
Since $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x) \equiv \neg P(x) \lor Q(x),$ the corresponding truth sets can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} T_{P \Rightarrow Q} &= T_{\neg P \lor Q} \\[5pt] &= T_{\neg P} \cup T_Q \\[5pt] &= \overline{T}_P \cup T_Q \end{align*}

Now, we note the following:

  • To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} 4x - 7 &\geq 9 \\[5pt] 4x &\geq 16 \\[5pt] x &\geq 4 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is $ T_P = [4,\infty). $ As a result, the complement is $ \overline{T}_P = (-\infty,4). $

  • The truth set of $Q(x)$ is $ T_Q = (0,5). $

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_{P \Rightarrow Q} &= \overline{T}_P \cup T_Q \\[5pt] &= (-\infty,4) \cup (0,5) \\[5pt] &= (-\infty,5). \end{align*}

question.text:
For the universal set $U,$ given by

\[ U = \big\{ 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10 \big\}, \]

find the truth set of $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x)$ for the following predicates:

  • $P(x):$ $x$ is composite.

  • $Q(x):$ $10$ is divisible by $x.$
question.explanation:
Since $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x) \equiv \neg P(x) \lor Q(x),$ the corresponding truth sets can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} T_{P \Rightarrow Q} &= T_{\neg P \lor Q} \\[5pt] &= T_{\neg P} \cup T_Q \\[5pt] &= \overline{T}_P \cup T_Q \end{align*}

Now, we note the following:

  • The truth set of $P(x)$ is \[ T_P = \left\{ 4,6,8,9,10 \right\}. \] As a result, the complement is \begin{align*} \overline{T}_P &= \overline{\big\{ 4,6,8,9,10 \big\}} \\[5pt] &= \big\{ 2,3,5,7 \big\}. \end{align*}

  • The truth set of $Q(x)$ is \[ T_Q = \big\{ 2,5,10 \big\}. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_{P \Rightarrow Q} &= \overline{T}_P \cup T_Q \\[5pt] &= \big\{ 2,3,5,7 \big\} \cup \big\{ 2,5,10 \big\} \\[5pt] &= \big\{ 2,3,5,7,10 \big\}. \end{align*}

question.text:
Find the truth set of $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $\mathbb{R}{:}$

  • $P(x):$ $3x - 1 \lt 5$

  • $Q(x):$ $x^2 \lt 4$
question.explanation:
Since $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x) \equiv \neg P(x) \lor Q(x),$ the corresponding truth sets can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} T_{P \Rightarrow Q} &= T_{\neg P \lor Q} \\[5pt] &= T_{\neg P} \cup T_Q \\[5pt] &= \overline{T}_P \cup T_Q \end{align*}

Now, we note the following:

  • To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} 3x - 1 &\lt 5 \\[5pt] 3x &\lt 6 \\[5pt] x &\lt 2 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is $ T_P = (-\infty,2). $ As a result, the complement is $ \overline{T}_P = [2,\infty). $

  • To find the the truth set of $Q(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} x^2 &\lt 4 \\[5pt] -2 &\lt x \lt 2 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $Q(x)$ is $ T_Q = (-2,2). $

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_{P \Rightarrow Q} &= \overline{T}_P \cup T_Q \\[5pt] &= [2,\infty) \cup (-2,2) \\[5pt] &= (-2,\infty). \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Truth Set of an Equivalence

question.text:
For the universal set $U,$ given by

\[ U = \big\{ 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 \big\}, \]

find the truth set of $P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x)$ for the following predicates:

  • $P(x):$ $x$ is prime.

  • $Q(x):$ $3\,|\,x.$
question.explanation:
Since we have that

\[ P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x) \equiv \big(P(x) \land Q(x)\big) \lor \big(\neg P(x) \land \neg Q(x)\big), \] the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} = (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q) \end{align*}

Notice that:

  • The truth set of $P(x)$ is \[ T_P = \big\{ 2,3,5,7 \big\} \] and its complement is \[ \overline{T}_P %= \overline{\big\{ 4,6,8,9,10 \big\}} = \big\{ 4,6,8,9 \big\}. \]

  • The truth set of $Q(x)$ is \[ T_Q = \big\{ 3,6,9 \big\} \] and its complement is \[ \overline{T}_Q %= \overline{\big\{ 2,5,10 \big\}} = \big\{ 2,4,5,7,8 \big\}. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_P \cap T_Q &= \big\{ 2,3,5,7 \big\} \cap \big\{ 3,6,9 \big\} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 3 \big\} \\[10pt] \overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q &= \big\{ 4,6,8,9 \big\} \cap \big\{ 2,4,5,7,8 \big\} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 4,8 \big\} \\[10pt] T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} &= (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q)\\[3pt] &= \big\{ 3 \big\} \cup \big\{ 4,8 \big\} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 3,4,8 \big\}. \end{align*}

question.text:
Find the truth set of $P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $\mathbb{R}{:}$

  • $P(x):$ $x^2 \leq 9$

  • $Q(x):$ $5x - 3 \gt 7$
question.explanation:
Since we have that

\[ P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x) \equiv \big(P(x) \land Q(x)\big) \lor \big(\neg P(x) \land \neg Q(x)\big), \]

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} = (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q) \end{align*}

Now, we note the following:

  • To find the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} x^2 &\leq 9 \\[5pt] -3 &\leq x \leq 3 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is $ T_P = [-3,3] . $ As a result, the complement is $ \overline{T}_P = (-\infty,-3)\cup(3,\infty). $
  • To find the truth set of $Q(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} 5x - 3 &\gt 7 \\[5pt] 5x &\gt 10 \\[5pt] x &\gt 2 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $Q(x)$ is $ T_Q = (2,\infty), $ and its complement is $ \overline{T}_Q = (-\infty,2]. $

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_P \cap T_Q &= [-3,3] \cap (2,\infty) \\[5pt] &= (2,3] \\[10pt] \overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q &= \big( (-\infty,-3)\cup(3,\infty) \big) \cap (-\infty,2] \\[5pt] &= (-\infty,-3) \\[10pt] T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} &= (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q)\\[5pt] &= (2,3] \cup (-\infty,-3) \\[5pt] &= (-\infty,-3) \cup (2,3]. \end{align*}

question.text:
Find the truth set of $P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $\mathbb{R}{:}$

  • $P(x):$ $3x - 1 \lt 5$

  • $Q(x):$ $x^2 \lt 4$
question.explanation:
Since we have that

\[ P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x) \equiv \big(P(x) \land Q(x)\big) \lor \big(\neg P(x) \land \neg Q(x)\big), \]

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} = (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q) \end{align*}

Now, we note the following:

  • To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} 3x - 1 &\lt 5 \\[5pt] 3x &\lt 6 \\[5pt] x &\lt 2 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is $ T_P = (-\infty,2). $ As a result, the complement is $ \overline{T}_P = [2,\infty). $

  • To find the the truth set of $Q(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} x^2 &\lt 4 \\[5pt] -2 &\lt x \lt 2 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $Q(x)$ is $ T_Q = (-2,2) $ and its complement is $ \overline{T}_Q = (-\infty,-2]\cup [2,\infty). $

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_P \cap T_Q &= (-\infty,2) \cap (-2,2) \\[5pt] &= (-2,2) \\[10pt] \overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q &=[2,\infty) \cap \big( (-\infty,-2]\cup [2,\infty)\big) \\[5pt] &= [2,\infty) \\[10pt] T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} &= (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q)\\[5pt] &= (-2,2) \cup [2,\infty) \\[5pt] &= (-2,\infty) . \end{align*}

question.text:
$\qquad$ If $x$ has more than three divisors, then $x$ is composite.

Which of the following is logically equivalent to the conditional predicate above?
question.choice1: $x$ doesn't have more than three divisors, or $x$ is composite.
question.choice2: $x$ doesn't have more than three divisors, and $x$ is composite.
question.choice3: $x$ has more than three divisors, or $x$ is composite.
question.choice4: $x$ has more than three divisors, and $x$ is composite.
question.choice5: $x$ doesn't have more than three divisors, or $x$ is not composite.
question.explanation:
Let's denote by $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ the following predicates:

  • $P(x){:}$ $x$ has more than three divisors.

  • $Q(x){:}$ $x$ is composite.

Then, our initial sentence can be written as $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x),$ which is logically equivalent to

\[ \neg P(x) \lor Q(x). \]

The negation of $P(x)$ can be written as

  • $\neg P(x){:}$ $x$ doesn't have more than three divisors.

Therefore, the given sentence is logically equivalent to the following:

$\qquad$ $x$ doesn't have more than three divisors, or $x$ is composite.

example.title: Using Laws Involving Implications and Equivalences

question.text:
Consider the following predicates.

$\qquad$ $A(x):$ $x\geq 2.$ $\qquad$ $B(x):$ $-x\leq -2.$

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate $A(x) \Leftrightarrow B(x)?$

  1. If $x\geq 2$ then $-x\leq -2,$ and if $-x\leq -2$ then $x \geq 2.$
  2. $x\geq 2$ is equivalent to $-x\leq -2.$
  3. If $x\geq 2$ then $-x\leq -2,$ or if $-x\leq -2$ then $x \geq 2.$
question.explanation:
A biconditional expression $P \Leftrightarrow Q \equiv (P \Rightarrow Q) \land (Q \Rightarrow P)$ can be read as shown below:

  • $P$ if and only if $Q$

  • $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

  • If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

So, $A \Leftrightarrow B$ translates into the following sentences:

  • $x\geq 2$ if and only if $-x\leq -2.$

  • $x\geq 2$ is equivalent to $-x\leq -2.$

  • If $x\geq 2$ then $-x\leq -2,$ and if $-x\leq -2$ then $x\geq 2.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
